# action.docker_compose_pull

<!-- Code generated by tools/genskill from the provider schema. DO NOT EDIT. -->

Kind: action. Back to [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md).

Pulls the image of every service of a compose project, like `docker compose pull`, with the provider's `registry_auth`. Services that only build (no `image`) and services with `pull_policy: build` are skipped (CLI `--ignore-buildable`). `result.pull_status` says what happened per service.

Actions need Terraform >= 1.14. They keep no state: they run when a
resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { ... } }` fires, or on demand with
`terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_pull.<name>`. Arguments go inside
the action's `config` block.

## Usage

```terraform
action "docker_compose_pull" "<name>" {
  config {
    # arguments below
  }
}

# Run it: lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [after_create] actions = [action.docker_compose_pull.<name>] } }
# on a resource, or: terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_pull.<name>
```

## Arguments and attributes

| Name | Type | Status | Forces replacement | Sensitive | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | `string` | optional |  |  | Compose YAML as a string. Exactly one of `content` and `files` must be set. |
| `env` | `map(string)` | optional |  |  | Variables for `${VAR}` interpolation. The provider's own environment is never read; values here override `env_file`. |
| `env_file` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Dotenv files read for interpolation variables (CLI `--env-file`), later files winning. |
| `files` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Compose file paths, merged in order like repeated `docker compose -f`. |
| `name` | `string` | optional |  |  | The compose project name (compose-spec top-level `name`, CLI `--project-name`). Defaults to the file's top-level `name`, then to the project directory's name. |
| `profiles` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Profiles to enable (CLI `--profile`). |
| `project_directory` | `string` | optional |  |  | The project directory relative paths resolve against (CLI `--project-directory`). Defaults to the first file's directory, or the Terraform working directory for `content`. |
| `result_path` | `string` | optional |  |  | Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails. |
| `services` | `list(string)` | optional |  |  | Only these services (default: every service of the project). |

## Example

```terraform
resource "docker_compose" "shop" {
  name    = "shop"
  content = <<-EOT
    services:
      web:
        image: nginx:1.27-alpine
        ports: ["8080:80"]
      worker:
        image: busybox:1.36
        command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
  EOT

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_compose_pull.this]
    }
  }
}

# Pulls every service image again (new digests are picked up by the next
# docker_compose apply). On demand:
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_compose_pull.this
action "docker_compose_pull" "this" {
  config {
    name    = "shop"
    content = docker_compose.shop.content
  }
}
```
